checks.description: orders primary key is unique and nonnull
checks.sql:
SELECT
  k0,
  COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.id AS k0
  FROM orders AS o
) AS gc_keys
GROUP BY
  k0
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 1 OR k0 IS NULL;

checks.description: input grain is unique and nonnull
checks.sql:

  k0,
  COUNT(*) AS occurrences

  SELECT
    o.id AS k0
  FROM orders AS o
) AS gc_keys
GROUP BY

checks.description: right join keys are unique (ordinary = ignores NULL keys)
checks.sql:
SELECT
  k0,
  COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM (
  SELECT
    c.id AS k0
  FROM customers AS c
) AS gc_keys
WHERE
  NOT k0 IS NULL
GROUP BY
  k0
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 1;

checks.description: each left grain matches at most one right row
checks.sql:
SELECT
  k0,
  COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.id AS k0
  FROM orders AS o
  INNER JOIN customers AS c
    ON o.customer_id = c.id
) AS gc_keys
WHERE
  NOT k0 IS NULL
GROUP BY
  k0
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 1;

checks.description: join preserves the left input row count
checks.sql:
SELECT
  *
FROM (
  SELECT
    (
      SELECT
        COUNT(*)
      FROM (
        SELECT
          1
        FROM orders AS o
      ) AS gc_before
    ) AS expected_rows,
    (
      SELECT
        COUNT(*)
      FROM (
        SELECT
          1
        FROM orders AS o
        LEFT JOIN customers AS c
          ON o.customer_id = c.id
      ) AS gc_after
    ) AS actual_rows
) AS gc_counts
WHERE
  expected_rows <> actual_rows;

checks.description: join preserves every left input grain, including multiplicity
checks.sql:
SELECT
  k0,
  SUM(before_rows) AS expected_rows,
  SUM(after_rows) AS actual_rows
FROM (
  SELECT
    k0,
    COUNT(*) AS before_rows,
    0 AS after_rows
  FROM (
    SELECT
      o.id AS k0
    FROM orders AS o
  ) AS gc_before
  GROUP BY
    k0
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    k0,
    0 AS before_rows,
    COUNT(*) AS after_rows
  FROM (
    SELECT
      o.id AS k0
    FROM orders AS o
    LEFT JOIN customers AS c
      ON o.customer_id = c.id
  ) AS gc_after
  GROUP BY
    k0
) AS gc_bag
GROUP BY
  k0
HAVING
  SUM(before_rows) <> SUM(after_rows);

checks.description: complete model output grain is unique and nonnull
checks.sql:
SELECT
  k0,
  COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM (
  SELECT
    order_id AS k0
  FROM (
    SELECT
      o.id AS order_id,
      c.name AS customer_name,
      o.amount
    FROM orders AS o
    LEFT JOIN customers AS c
      ON o.customer_id = c.id
  ) AS gc_model
) AS gc_keys
GROUP BY
  k0
HAVING
  COUNT(*) > 1 OR k0 IS NULL;
